Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the run chase. The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Rachin Ravindra and Will Young will be the two openers for the New Zealand. Asitha Fernando has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

The New Zealand bowlers were exceptional, displaying discipline to restrict Sri Lanka's scoring. Matt Henry was the standout performer, delivering a miserly spell of 10 overs, conceding just 19 runs, and claiming 4 crucial wickets. The supporting cast of Jacob Duffy and Nathan Smith chipped in with 2 wickets each, while Mitchell Santner contributed with a solitary scalp, rounding out a dominant bowling display by the Kiwis.

The Sri Lankan top order struggled to find their footing, with Avishka Fernando being the sole exception. The visitors lost a cluster of wickets in quick succession, which derailed their innings. Janith Liyanage, Wanindu Hasaranga, and Chamindu Karunaratne showed promise, but unfortunately, they were unable to capitalize on their starts. Avishka Fernando scored a brilliant half-century but perished on 56 being the top-scorer of the side.
We've reached the midway point, and New Zealand are undoubtedly pleased with their efforts so far. They've made the most of the favorable conditions, restricting Sri Lanka to a modest total of 178.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for play to begin now. The umpire stride out in the middle followed by the players of New Zealand led by Mitchell Santner. Pathum Nissanka and Avishka Fernando walk out as the visitors' opening pair while Matt Henry will bowl the first over of this contest.

We are all set for the pre-match formalities. The teams are lining up in the middle for their respective National Anthems. The proceedings will begin with the National Anthem of Sri Lanka, followed by the National Anthem of New Zealand.

Charith Asalanka, the skipper of Sri Lanka says they would have loved to bowl first as well. Mentions that they are going in with a 7-5 combo having three seamers and Eshan Malinga makes his ODI debut.Reckons that the last T20I win has helped them in terms of momentum and they'll look to cash in.

Mitchell Santner, the skipper of New Zealand says the pitch was under cover for a couple of days so there will be moisture underneath and they'll look to use it to a good effect. Mentions that the pitch is going to be a good one but the wind is going to be a massive factor. Informs that Tom Latham has a niggle and Mitchell Hay is in for him.

As always, expect plenty of excitement, fierce competition, and maybe a few surprises on the field. Let’s see who takes the first step towards ODI glory! Toss and team news to follow shortly...

Meanwhile, Sri Lanka aims to turn the tide overseas, having not won an ODI series in New Zealand since 2001. Charith Asalanka and his squad are ready to prove they can perform away from home, despite a recent string of successes on home soil.
After clinching the T20I series 2-1, captain Mitchell Santner is eager to continue the winning momentum from the T20I series, bolstered by the return of seasoned batters Tom Latham and Will Young.

Hello cricket fans! Get ready for an exciting showdown as New Zealand takes on Sri Lanka in the first ODI of a thrilling three-match series at the Basin Reserve in Hamilton! With the stadium buzzing and crowd ready to cheer, we're set for an unforgettable day of cricket.
... MATCHDAY ...

It is time for the ODI leg of Sri Lanka's white-ball tour of New Zealand, and with the Champions Trophy just around the corner, this leg carries added significance. The Cello Basin Reserve in Wellington will host the first ODI before the caravan moves to Hamilton and Auckland for the remaining two matches.  The hosts enter the series on the back of a 2-1 T20I series win but are not at full strength, with a few senior players occupied with franchise league commitments. This marks Mitchell Santner's first ODI assignment as full-time captain. The experienced left-arm spinner will lead the spin department alongside Michael Bracewell. Jacob Duffy, fresh from an impressive T20I series, will continue in the longer format, supported by Matt Henry and the promising William O'Rourke in the pace attack. ODI specialists Will Young and Tom Latham strengthen the squad, while Daryl Mitchell, Rachin Ravindra, and Glenn Phillips add depth to an experienced batting unit. For Sri Lanka, the win in the final T20I would have boosted their confidence, and they will be eager to translate that momentum into success in this crucial ODI series. Like the hosts, the tourists retain a largely similar batting unit from the T20I series. Pathum Nissanka will be key again, while Charith Asalanka, Avishka Fernando, Kamindu Mendis, and Kusal Mendis will aim to deliver with the Champions Trophy looming. The changes for Sri Lanka come in the bowling department, particularly in the pace unit, where Asitha Fernando and Lahiru Kumara bring experience and firepower to the attack. In the spin department, Wanindu Hasaranga and Maheesh Theekshana retain their spots from the T20I series, while the additions of Dunith Wellalage and Jeffrey Vandersay provide depth and variety. It was in 2001 when the Asian side last won a bilateral ODI series on New Zealand soil. Can they start with a win and take a step towards breaking that long-standing streak? We shall find out.
